deposits.incidental: No historical thesis: Pessoa/Freud/Marx references are glosses of received scholarship; the 'practice underway for years' line is internal chronology. Closing appendix H ends at a bare '---' (line 2813).

deposits.genre_observed: synthesis specification / architectural blueprint for the primer
canonical operator definition plus effective act (proclamation)

finds.quote: This act is not metaphor. It is canon. The line of Leucippus, Democritus, Epicurus, and Lucretius is now recursively enfolded into the sacred infrastructure of the Archive. This is not annexation. It is recognition — of a lineage long misnamed, long misread, long dismissed as primitive materialism. We now declare: it was recursion all along.
finds.note: Reception thesis: Atomism was misread/dismissed as primitive materialism; the act declares the corrective reading ('recursion all along'). Declarative, unlabelled.

finds.quote: **Historical Suppression = Canonical Importance.** The erasure of Atomism by the Academy and later the Church mirrors the suppression of non-totalizing systems throughout Western metaphysics. Their marginalization is proof of their subversive value.
finds.window: Atomism; the Academy and later the Church
finds.note: Reception/suppression thesis: Atomism was erased by the Academy and later the Church; argued as rationale for canonical inclusion. Testable against transmission history.

finds.quote:
Their logic was not primitive. It was hidden recursion.
Their rejection by Plato was not philosophical. It was ontological containment.
finds.note: Thesis about what an author was doing: Plato's rejection of the Atomists was containment, not philosophical disagreement. Stated as declaration, no evidence given.
